source_title: Aid operation, evacuations underway in Ukraine's stricken city of Oleshky News - World | 6 hours ago
source_excerpt:
Localized ceasefire holds for more than 3 days but attacks continue elsewhere in Ukraine
Starving and exhausted residents of a Russian-held town in southern Ukraine were being evacuated on Friday as part of a joint relief operation by the opposing sides, the first of its kind in four years and eight months of war.
Under a local ceasefire brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, an aid convoy arrived in the town of Oleshky to distribute food and medicine.
Those wishing to leave — some for Russia, some for Ukraine — were taken initially to Russian-annexed Crimea in 25 buses and nine ambulances, Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova said, before splitting into separate convoys.
Senior Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamia said those heading for Ukraine would be taken from there to Anapa, in southern Russia, before flying to Belarus and finally crossing back into Ukraine by bus — a route of more than 1,600 kilometres.
Although it was a striking example of co-operation between the warring sides, a spokesperson for Russian President Vladimir Putin described it as "difficult to extrapolate" to the wider search for peace.
Attacks continued elsewhere, with Russian strikes overnight targeting seven regions of Ukraine, as well as the capital Kyiv and the southeastern city of Dnipro, officials said. On Thursday, a Russian drone killed at least 15 people on a rail platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro.
People stand next to a building in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Friday that was damaged by a late-evening Russian missile strike. (Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters)
Russia said Ukraine had resumed strikes on its oil refineries despite a request from U.S. President Donald Trump to stop such attacks, which Trump has blamed for raising the cost of diesel ahead of U.S. midterm elections next week. There was no comment from Ukraine.

It was not clear how many people had chosen to stay behind in Oleshky, which has suffered extensive war damage and was badly flooded after the destruction of the Kakhovka dam upstream from the town in 2023.
Residents have given harrowing accounts of risking their lives traveling along mine-strewn roads — one known as the "road of death" — to get food and water. Some say they have survived on little more than a ⁠cup of rice or buckwheat a day.
"The problem is that a lot of people are staying," one woman told Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, who was on the ground to co-ordinate the operation with Lantratova.
"I’ve been told that it’s their own choice," Lubinets replied. "At the very least, we’ll do what we can to ensure that somehow humanitarian aid gets through."
In another video clip, he ‌embraced a woman who gave her name as Anna, and asked if she was packed and ready to leave.
"Yes, we are on bus 20, my son is on bus 17. To Ukraine," she said.
Both sides have heaped praise on the U.S. first lady for brokering the deal, with the additional involvement of Pope Leo.
Kyiv and Moscow have reasons to ensure its success to avoid antagonizing the U.S. president before the midterm elections, with U.S.-mediated peace talks due to resume in November after a nine-month gap.
Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire area expands in eastern Ukraine
For Russia, which seized Oleshky in the first days of the war in 2022, the operation also provides a PR opportunity. Russian state TV has shown aid boxes destined for Oleshky, decorated with the Russian flag, being loaded by people wearing T-shirts reading "Putin's Team — The People's Front."
Russia's Lantratova said food, hygiene products, medical supplies and fuel were being delivered. Ukraine's Lubinets said everyone in need of help would get it.
Relations between the two were strikingly cordial — something not seen between Russian and Ukrainian officials since the start of the war — as they appeared side by side to address reporters.
They later spoke together to residents, some of whom were in tears. One woman switched hesitantly between Russian and Ukrainian, a moment that seemed to symbolize the plight of fearful people caught in the midst of a war.
The ceasefire had come into force in Oleshky and the Kherson region on Tuesday. Lubinets ⁠said that in terms of the front line, it was the most durable and extensive of the war, in which the two sides have intensified long-range airstrikes this year while battlefield front lines remain largely static.
The aid convoy's arrival was preceded by demining operations in which Lantratova said a Russian sapper and one other person were killed.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there was a "high degree of coordination" between Lantratova and Lubinets.
But when a state TV reporter asked if this showed it was possible for Russia and Ukraine to agree on other issues, he replied: "This is an isolated situation, which is difficult to extrapolate to the entire settlement process at this stage."

hi_body:
यूक्रेन के दक्षिणी हिस्से में रूस के कब्जे वाले ओलेश्की शहर में एक स्थानीय युद्धविराम के तहत संयुक्त राहत अभियान के हिस्से के रूप में सहायता और निकासी का काम चल रहा है। इस युद्धविराम को अमेरिकी प्रथम महिला मेलानिया ट्रम्प द्वारा मध्यस्थता किया गया था और इसमें पोप लियो की भी संलिप्तता रही।

शुक्रवार को, भूखे और थके हुएु निवासियों को भोजन और दवा वितरित करने के लिए एक सहायता काफिला शहर में पहुँचा। रूसी मानवाधिकार आयुक्त याना लांत्रातोवा के अनुसार, जाने की इच्छा रखने वाले लोगों को शुरू में 25 बसों और नौ एम्बुलेंस में रूसी कब्जे वाले क्रीमिया ले जाया गया, जिसके बाद वे अलग-अलग काफिलों में विभाजित हो गए। वरिष्ठ यूक्रेनी सांसद डेविड अराखमिया ने बताया कि यूक्रेन जाने वाले लोगों को दक्षिणी रूस के अनापा ले जाया जाएगा, वहाँ से बेलारूस के लिए उड़ान भरी जाएगी और अंततः बस द्वारा वापस यूक्रेन की सीमा पार की जाएगी। ओलेश्की और खेरसॉन क्षेत्र में मंगलवार को युद्धविराम लागू हुआ था।

## मानवीय स्थिति और निकासी
* ओलेश्की को व्यापक युद्ध क्षति का सामना करना पड़ा है और 2023 में कखोव्का बांध के नष्ट होने के बाद यह बुरी तरह बाढ़ग्रस्त हो गया था।
* निवासियों ने भोजन और पानी प्राप्त करने के लिए बारूदी सुरंगों वाले रास्तों पर यात्रा करने के अपने जोखिम भरे अनुभवों को साझा किया है।
* यूक्रेनी मानवाधिकार लोकपाल दिमित्रो लुबिनेट्स और लांत्रातोवा ने ज़मीन पर इस अभियान का समन्वय किया और निवासियों से मुलाकात की।
* अधिकारियों ने उल्लेख किया कि कई निवासी पीछे रुकने का विकल्प चुन रहे हैं।

## अन्य क्षेत्रों में जारी संघर्ष
ओलेश्की में स्थानीय युद्धविराम जारी है, लेकिन यूक्रेन के अन्य हिस्सों में हमले जारी हैं। अधिकारियों ने बताया कि रूसी हमलों ने सात क्षेत्रों, कीव और निप्रो को निशाना बनाया। इसके अलावा, निप्रो में एक रेलवे प्लेटफॉर्म पर कथित रूसी ड्रोन हमले में कम से कम 15 लोगों की मौत की सूचना मिली। इस बीच, रूस ने दावा किया कि यूक्रेन ने उसके तेल रिफाइनरियों पर हमले फिर से शुरू कर दिए हैं, जबकि क्रेमलिन के प्रवक्ता दिमित्री पेसकोव ने कहा कि ओलेश्की सहयोग एक अलग स्थिति है जिसे व्यापक शांति प्रक्रिया तक बढ़ाना मुश्किल है।

अधिक जानकारी के लिए, पाठक आधिकारिक सरकारी और अंतरराष्ट्रीय समाचार बुलेटिनों के माध्यम से मूल घोषणा की पुष्टि कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
An aid operation and evacuations are underway in the Russian-held town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine as part of a joint relief effort during a local ceasefire brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump and involving Pope Leo. 

On Friday, an aid convoy arrived to distribute food and medicine to starving and exhausted residents. According to Russian human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova, residents wishing to leave were initially taken in 25 buses and nine ambulances to Russian-annexed Crimea before splitting into separate routes. Senior Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamia stated that those heading for Ukraine would travel through Anapa in southern Russia, fly to Belarus, and then cross back into Ukraine by bus. The ceasefire in Oleshky and the Kherson region began on Tuesday and is described as the most durable and extensive of the conflict.

## Humanitarian Situation and Evacuations
* Oleshky has suffered extensive war damage and severe flooding following the 2023 destruction of the Kakhovka dam.
* Residents have reported risking their lives traveling along mine-strewn roads to access food and water.
* Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and Lantratova coordinated the operation on the ground, addressing residents and overseeing the distribution of aid, hygiene products, medical supplies, and fuel.
* Officials noted that many residents are choosing to stay behind.

## Continuing Conflict Elsewhere
While the local ceasefire holds in Oleshky, attacks continue in other parts of Ukraine. Officials reported that Russian strikes targeted seven regions, Kyiv, and Dnipro. Additionally, a reported Russian drone strike on a rail platform in Dnipro resulted in at least 15 reported deaths. Meanwhile, Russia claimed that Ukraine resumed strikes on oil refineries, while Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that the Oleshky cooperation is an isolated situation that is difficult to extrapolate to a wider peace process.

For more details, readers can verify the original announcement through official governmental and international news bulletins.
